title: Perfect tensor tests preserve quasi-coherent homotopy inverse limits
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces with small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ an algebraic space which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: its point space is quasi-compact and its diagonal is quasi-compact. The affine spectrum is [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ is its full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ means etale locally a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Set $T_E(F)=R\Gamma(X,F\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}E)\in D(A)$, where tensor uses K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] and derived global sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] has its A-action through $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. This is an exact functor on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ which preserves products. More precisely, for any countable family $(F_n)$ in this subcategory the product exists there and the comparison $T_E(\prod^{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}_n F_n)\to\prod^{D(A)}_n T_E(F_n)$ induced by the projections is an isomorphism. Consequently, if $(F_n,t_n)$ is a strict tower of complexes representing objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $K$ is its homotopy inverse limit there, defined by the triangle $K\to\prod^{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}_nF_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod^{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}_nF_n\to K[1]$ [def-weil-derived-limit], then $T_E(K)$ is isomorphic in $D(A)$ to $R\varprojlim_nT_E(F_n)$. The isomorphism can be chosen to identify the arrows to the products in the two defining triangles. Products in the source are taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, rather than assumed to agree with ambient products.

proof.text: Check the hypotheses of the general tensor-test lemma. By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], the quasi-compact point space of $X$ supplies a surjective affine etale atlas. By [lem-sfb-etale-affine-pairs-test-quasiseparated], its quasi-compact absolute diagonal gives the affine-chart-pair condition for the derived coherator. The affine base is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] makes $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finally [lem-sfb-space-perfect-uniform-tor] puts the given perfect $E$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Thus both the coherator and the general perfect-tensor global-sections lemma apply without a finite-type, properness or Noetherian assumption.

source.place: Tag 0CR4, lemma-better-coherator; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08JL, lemma-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: Use the equivalent small ringed model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. For any set-indexed family $F_j$, choose K-injective representatives $J_j$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The termwise product $J=\prod_jJ_j$ exists: module-sheaf products are objectwise products, with differential the coordinate differentials. A map from an acyclic complex to $J$ has coordinate null-homotopies; their product is a null-homotopy, so $J$ is K-injective. Chain maps into $J$, and homotopies between them, are coordinate families. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(N,J)$ with $\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(N,J_j)$, naturally in $N$. This constructs an ambient derived product $P_{\mathrm{amb}}$ without asserting it is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products, product construction; derived.tex Tag 0BK6, lemma-product-K-injective, coordinate homotopy argument written out.

proof.text: Write $I:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}\hookrightarrow D(\mathcal O_X)$ and use its right adjoint $DQ_X$ from [lem-sfb-space-derived-coherator-adjunction]. For $F_j\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, set $P=DQ_X(P_{\mathrm{amb}})$, using the ambient product of Step 2. For every $G\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ the adjunction and fullness give $\operatorname{Hom}(G,P)=\operatorname{Hom}(IG,P_{\mathrm{amb}})=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(IG,IF_j)=\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(G,F_j)$. The projections are the counit followed by the ambient projections. This is precisely the product universal property, so the required source products exist in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$.

source.place: Tag 0CR4, lemma-better-coherator; elementary application of its adjunction to ambient products.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-tensor-global-limits] with $f$, $E$ and the products of Step 3. Its functor $F_E$ is exactly the stated $T_E$, with the same structure-induced $A$-action, K-flat tensor and derived global sections. It is exact and its product comparison is an isomorphism for every family in the indexing universe. Its components are $T_E(\operatorname{pr}_j)$, so this is the comparison required in the item, including the countable case. This is a use of an existing more general node, not a newly introduced reformulation of the item.

source.place: Tag 0CX6, lemma-compute-against-perfect, global derived Hom paragraph and final translation by sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JJ.

proof.text: For the given tower write $P=\prod_n^{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}F_n$, $p:K\to P$, $q_n=\operatorname{pr}_np$, and let $c:T_E(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nT_E(F_n)$ be Step 4. The product-triangle clause of [lem-sfb-space-perfect-tensor-global-limits] makes the triangle with first arrow $cT_E(p)$ and middle arrow $1-s^{\prime}$ distinguished, where $\operatorname{pr}_ns^{\prime}=T_E(t_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Explicitly, composing $cT_E(s)$ and $s^{\prime}c$ with $\operatorname{pr}_n$ gives in both cases $T_E(t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})$; additivity therefore carries $1-s$ to $1-s^{\prime}$. By [def-weil-derived-limit] this triangle exhibits $T_E(K)$ as a derived limit. Now let $(R,p^{\prime},\delta^{\prime})$ be any derived limit of $(T_E(F_n),T_E(t_n))$, which is what $R\varprojlim_nT_E(F_n)$ denotes. The final clause of the same node gives an isomorphism $\varphi:T_E(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ with $\operatorname{pr}_np^{\prime}\varphi=T_E(q_n)=\operatorname{pr}_ncT_E(p)$ for every $n$. By the universal property of the product, $p^{\prime}\varphi=cT_E(p)$: under $c$, $\varphi$ identifies the arrows to the products of the two defining triangles. No functorial or unique choice of the isomorphism is claimed.
